data.why: The repo already ships a processed prototype dataset (data/processed/water_risk_with_rainfall.csv) and a bundled sample CSV, but app.py unconditionally reads data/processed/wqmis_up_2026_2027_risk.csv with no existence check, so that one file must be seeded or the dashboard crashes on load.

goals: Filter monitored villages by district and risk level to see which locations are CRITICAL or HIGH priority
Inspect the Folium risk map and intervention priority queue to decide where to send field inspection teams first
Drill into a single village's risk factors (water contamination, rainfall anomaly, groundwater stress, historical contamination, population exposure) to understand why it was flagged
Run a what-if rainfall scenario on a chosen village to see how simulated rainfall changes the explainable risk score and level
Review the verified government WQ6 contamination-indicator panel and compare it against the AI-fused risk layer
Check groundwater telemetry coverage and data-quality audit panels to judge how trustworthy the groundwater inputs are

review.summary: The tree follows the README's stated workflow closely: its phases, tasks and features are cut well, and all ten screens I opened show what their nodes claim. Before filing it needs a few fixes: the data note must say the WQ6 panel used seeded stand-in data, phase 5 overclaims a comparison the app says is impossible, and the rule-based vs AI-fused score comparison should be its own task.
